findings.label: PART 1 mechanism differs from the brief
findings.detail: The brief specified least-invasive affinity-based steering (podAntiAffinity/nodeAffinity preference); the implementation instead retires ComfyUI's Intel Arc workers via replicas: 0. This is justified by a confirmed storage-anchor blocker (comfy-xpu-worker pinned by a local-storage PV nodeAffinity to gremlin-1; intel-media holds a shared RWO Longhorn volume), aligns with the explicit user decision in the original messages, achieves the stated placement goal (gremlin-1 5/5->3/5 i915, no co-location of ComfyUI GPU pods with the embeddings replica, no Pending, all nodes <=5 i915), is reversible (Deployments kept at 0), and preserves the embeddings 1/node podAntiAffinity. Non-blocking.

findings.label: memirq root cause persists
findings.detail: The i915 SR-IOV VF memirq flood is a hardware-level issue not fixable in k8s; the embeddings crash-loop is resolved only at the tested load (8344 req/5min, 0 restarts). The tightened exec readiness probe is the durable client-facing mitigation (wedged replica leaves the LB in ~15s vs ~600s). Acknowledged by the author and acceptable under the brief's 'reduced not eliminated but invisible to clients' clause. Non-blocking; monitor under heavier contention.
